stories.headline: Winning, differently: On the by-election results in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry
stories.title: Winning, differently: On the by-election results in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry
stories.summary: Ruling parties sweep by-elections, but defections mar Tamil Nadu results
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'election results' in title weight 64
article_sentences: The by-election results in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, declared on Friday, held few surprises.
Barely five months after the April Assembly elections, the ruling party in each State/UT won all five bypolls.
What varied was the scale of victory.
In West Bengal, the BJP retained Nandigram and wrested Rejinagar, with strong vote shares of 76% and 63%.
In Puducherry, the ruling.
All India N.R. Congress also registered an emphatic win — 61% of the votes — in Thattanchavady.
Nandigram and Thattanchavady were vacated by the Chief Ministers, which partly explains the strong wins.
But the contests in Tamil Nadu were closer.
Dharapuram and Madurantakam fell vacant after their AIADMK MLAs resigned and defected to the ruling TVK, which renominated them.
Both won their seats back with 37% and 40% of the vote, respectively, leading the DMK rival candidates by about eight percentage points.
By-elections tend to favour the party in power, as voters prefer representatives with access to government.
But the variance between West Bengal and Tamil Nadu reflects the nature of contest in two similarly sized States but with vastly different political cultures.

stories.headline: 27 relief camps readied for residents of flood-prone areas in Sholinganallur and Perungudi
stories.title: 27 relief camps readied for residents of flood-prone areas in Sholinganallur and Perungudi
stories.summary: Minister K.Vignesh inspects monsoon preparedness in some of the most flood prone areas in the southern part of the city
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Excise and Prohibition Minister K. Vignesh on Monday reviewed the monsoon preparedness work in some of the most flood-prone areas in the southern parts of the city and ordered officials to expedite work on relief centres at 27 locations to help residents during the Northeast monsoon.
He also directed officials to complete work in three days.

Owing to the risk of heavy flooding in the southern parts of the city, the Minister directed the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) to expedite work on water supply, toilet facilities, power, and food for residents at relief centres.

The Minister ordered officials to prepare food for residents of flood-prone areas by facilitating the supply of food from 21 Amma Canteens in Perungudi, 17 Amma canteens in Sholinganallur, and six community kitchens.
The Minister advised.
THE GCC to appoint nodal officers to prepare the food for distribution.
He also directed officials to coordinate with fire and rescue services to catch snakes in flood-prone residential areas in the two zones during the monsoon.
In Sholinganallur zone, work on 95.7 km of drains has been completed.
Work on 13.385 km of drains is under way.
In Perungudi, 145.27 km of drains out of 154.19 km has been completed.
Work on 73 metres of drains in nine stretches is under way.
The Minister directed officials to expedite the work.

stories.headline: September retail inflation rises to 5.54 percent, food crosses 7 percent
stories.title: September retail inflation rises to 5.54 percent, food crosses 7 percent
stories.summary: India’s retail inflation climbed to 5.54 percent in September, its highest level so far this year, as vegetable and spice prices surged, according to government data released on Monday.Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, says the September print was lower than the bank’s projection of 5.7 percent. He expects inflation for the quarter to be 4.9 percent, in line with the Reserve Bank of India’s projection.“Risks remain tilted to the upside, owing to the sub-par and uneven monsoons, as well as crude oil prices,” says Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA.“As of now, higher inflation is mainly due to depletion of earlier stocks as we head to the new season. Crop arrivals are hence important,” Sabnavis explains.Food was the main driver. Food inflation rose to 7.74 percent from 5.97 percent in August. Meanwhile, the food and beverages division of the CPI basket recorded an inflation print of 7.36 percent.Also Read: Strait of Hormuz shows economic risk of geography: PK MishraOnion led the increase, with prices up 108.09 percent year-on-year, more than double the 48.78 percent recorded in August. Ginger rose 62.85 percent, garlic 54.62 percent and lemon 36.41 percent. Silver jewellery, whose prices were up 87.8 percent, eased from 106.81 percent a month earlier.Some items offered relief. Potato prices fell 11.5 percent and tomato prices fell 8.62 percent, although tomato’s decline narrowed sharply from 31.09 percent in August. Motor cars and jeeps were 4.51 percent cheaper, and lady’s finger and coconut also declined by 4.48 percent and 3.99 percent, respectively.However, pressure varied across geographies. Rural inflation stood at 6.08 percent, up from 5.24 percent in August, while urban inflation was 4.88 percent, up from 4.31 percent. The gap was wider for food, at 8.06 percent in rural areas against 7.18 percent in cities, reflecting the higher weightage of food in the rural index.Price pressures were not confined to food. Among the 12 divisions, personal care, social protection and services recorded the highest inflation at 13.75 percent, with the “other personal effects” group up 38.69 percent. The higher inflation in this category was “mainly due to silver and gold where prices are determined externally. These three categories will continue to exert pressure,” says Sabnavis.Restaurants and accommodation services followed at 9.36 percent, amid higher energy costs due to continuing disruptions linked to the war in West Asia, while transport services for goods rose 14.73 percent. Health showed the lowest inflation print at 1.40 percent, followed by recreation, sport and culture at 2.16 percent.Also Read: Nirmala Sitharaman: Global Economy Needs Resilience Amid UncertaintyAmong major states, Tamil Nadu recorded the highest headline inflation at 6.81 percent, followed by Odisha (6.70 percent), Madhya Pradesh (6.68 percent), Telangana (6.64 percent) and Andhra Pradesh (6.29 percent). Tamil Nadu also recorded a high food inflation rate of 10.62 percent, followed by Andhra Pradesh at 10.81 percent, Odisha (9.58 percent), Karnataka (9 percent) and Maharashtra (8.91 percent).Sabnavis adds that the transmission of higher wholesale prices into the CPI is yet to be seen. Durables, FMCG and automobile firms have announced price increases that should show up over the next few months. He warned that the third quarter of this fiscal year will be more challenging, with inflation peaking at 6 percent. “Our view still holds that December will warrant another rate hike,” he says.

stories.headline: Supreme Court wants cap on trade margin for all essential medicines and medical products
stories.title: Supreme Court wants cap on trade margin for all essential medicines and medical products
stories.summary: Government proposes 30% trade-margin cap on patented and non-patented cancer medicines, but top court asks why a margin cap cannot be extended to all medicines and medical products; the court says the government has to ensure that DPCO-approved medicines, whose price is legally regulated, reach patients
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Even as the Centre informed the Supreme Court on Monday (October 12, 2026) that it had decided to cap trade margins at 30% for non-scheduled cancer drugs, the court questioned why the benefit of such price regulation should be confined to cancer drugs and not extended to other essential medicines and medical products.

The development comes after a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta expressed concern over stark disparities between the price to retailer (PTR) and the maximum retail price (MRP) of certain medicines, particularly cancer drugs, with mark-ups in some instances soaring to 1,000%.
The Bench had flagged that such exorbitant mark-ups constituted “broad daylight dacoity” and placed an enormous financial burden on patients.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, informed the Bench that the proposed 30% trade-margin cap would cover both patented and non-patented cancer medicines, with an expert committee headed by the Director General of Health Services tasked with identifying the drugs to be brought within its ambit.
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) will examine the committee’s recommendations before issuing a price notification to implement the cap.

The Bench, however, said that while the intervention was commendable, it was inadequate, and questioned why other medicines and medical devices could not also be brought within the 16% retailer margin prescribed under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013.
“This is just the tip of the iceberg...
this has come around only because of the unduly hard observations we made during earlier hearings.
What about other drugs,” the Bench asked.

The top court was hearing petitions filed by advocate Kishan Chand Jain and paediatric surgeon Sanjay Kulshrestha seeking stricter enforcement of price controls under the DPCO to curb disproportionate margins across the pharmaceutical supply chain.

Justice Mehta drew attention to steep markups on medical devices and consumables, pointing out that an India-made cardiac stent costing around ₹5,000 was being sold by hospitals for more than ₹25,000.
He cited the example of a saline drip line carrying an MRP of ₹11 being sold for ₹270.

stories.headline: BJP urges INDIA alliance to put national interest above politics
stories.title: BJP urges INDIA alliance to put national interest above politics
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 12: Jammu and Kashmir BJP Chief Spokesperson and Senior Advocate Sunil Sethi on Monday urged the INDIA Alliance to prioritise national interest over political confrontation, stressing that democratic opposition must not compromise national security, institutional stability or public order. Sethi said every political party had the democratic right to oppose the government, question its policies and organise peaceful protests. However, he maintained that such opposition must be exercised responsibly and should not undermine public confidence in democratic institutions. Expressing concern over the growing politicisation of issues related to national security, constitutional institutions and India's international standing, Sethi said political parties must ensure that internal divisions and disagreements were not exploited by forces hostile to the country. He called upon the INDIA Alliance leadership to clarify its position on national security, public order and institutional stability amid political confrontations. “Opposition to a government is a democratic right, but safeguarding the nation is a responsibility shared by every political party,” Sethi said, adding that political differences must not compromise India's security, sovereignty or constitutional institutions. Sethi also said allegations of coordination between domestic political actors and forces hostile to India were serious matters that required credible evidence. Any instance of unlawful collaboration, foreign interference or incitement to violence, he added, should be investigated by the competent authorities in accordance with law. Emphasising the distinction between peaceful dissent and unlawful conduct, Sethi said democratic protests were constitutional rights, but violence, intimidation and deliberate disruption of public order could not be justified in the name of political opposition. He also questioned whether the INDIA Alliance was giving adequate attention to constructive policy alternatives on employment, economic development, public welfare and national security, arguing that political confrontation should not overshadow substantive public issues. Referring to Jammu and Kashmir, Sethi said the region's experience underlined the importance of public confidence, communal harmony and a clear distinction between democratic disagreement and activities that threaten national security. He urged political parties to exercise restraint while commenting on sensitive security matters and avoid statements that could deepen social divisions. “Governments will come and go, political alliances will change, and electoral contests will continue. But the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India must remain beyond partisan bargaining,” Sethi said. He called for a responsible political discourse that allows vigorous opposition and constitutional accountability while safeguarding national security and democratic freedoms.

stories.title: Cabinet nod sought to extend power fund for 5 yrs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The fund finances projects that support the reliability, security and stability of India's electricity grid.
It is mainly used to support investments important to secure power-system operations that may not be commercially viable for utilities.
The union budget for FY27 earmarked around ₹1,103 crore for the PSDF.
The ministry did not respond to an email seeking comment until press time Monday.
The Cabinet approval for the 15th finance commission cycle of FY22-26 period came in July 2023, with an allocation of ₹11,000 crore.

As per regulations, regional power committees, electricity generation companies, transmission licensees, distribution licensees, load dispatch centres and public sector undertakings need to give details of the projects and schemes for funding from the PSDF.

Categories eligible for funding include transmission systems of strategic importance, reactive energy generators, standard and special protection schemes, pilot and demonstration projects, and renovation and modernisation of transmission and distribution systems.
As India's renewable energy capacity increases, the grid needs additional voltage support, storage and protection systems to manage variable generation.

According to a Crisil Ratings report in March, addition of renewable energy capacity amid slower deployment of transmission infrastructure poses a risk of grid curtailment for more than 35 GW of capacity in fiscal 2027.
This is largely because of a lack of long-term grid access.
Curtailment for prolonged duration can impact the equity internal rate of return and the debt service coverage ratio of projects, the report said.
